articles.title: Keeping Futhark off the GPU
articles.summary: Futhark's implementation of automatic differentiation for sparse Jacobian matrices involves coloring a graph corresponding to the sparsity pattern of a matrix, but this process is inherently sequential due to the need for in-place updates, which can be done efficiently on the CPU. However, the problem arises when trying to exploit parallel hardware like a GPU for the second step of the algorithm, which requires massive parallelism. The solution is to copy the array as a whole before the loop to amortize the communication cost, but this approach is not feasible when an index into the GPU array is used in the loop.
